title: Crash: Segmentation fault / Read access violation in SkeletonModificationStack2D due to dangling raw pointer
body:
### Tested versions

4.x (master branch)

### System information

Windows 11 - Godot v4.x (master branch) - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) / Vulkan - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 (Intel Core i5-12600KF)

### Issue description

When a scene containing a SkeletonModificationStack2D is reloaded, or when Skeleton2D / modification nodes are freed in the editor or during runtime, the engine frequently suffers a hard crash (segmentation fault / read access violation).

This happens due to a lifecycle mismatch between Resource and Node. The SkeletonModificationStack2D (which is a Resource) stores a raw pointer (Skeleton2D *skeleton) to the Skeleton2D node in the scene tree.

When the scene tree changes or the skeleton node is destroyed, the Resource persists in memory but the raw pointer is not cleared, becoming a dangling pointer. Immediately after the node is destroyed, if the editor attempts to update the viewport (calling set_editor_gizmos_dirty() or draw_editor_gizmos()) or if a modification attempts to execute, it dereferences the dangling skeleton pointer to call methods like skeleton->queue_redraw(). This results in an immediate crash accessing corrupted memory/hashes (e.g., 0x111017501110177).

### Steps to reproduce

Create a 2D scene with a Skeleton2D node and a SkeletonModificationStack2D attached.

Add and enable any 2D modification in the stack (e.g., SkeletonModification2DTwoBoneIK).

Make sure the modification is set to "Resource Local To Scene" (this often exacerbates the lifecycle issue).

Reload the scene by double-clicking it in the FileSystem dock, or free the skeleton nodes via code.

The engine immediately crashes with a segmentation fault due to the dangling pointer accessing invalid memory.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

No MRP attached since this is a clear code-level dangling pointer lifecycle issue verified during development. The issue can be reproduced with any basic 2D IK setup when the scene is forcefully reloaded or the skeleton is queued for deletion.
